text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbian opposition dealt blow: Further massive protests break out as court upholds scrapping of vote results.
- Airline to woo creditors, customers: Canadian Airlines seeking debt moratorium.
- Thousands booking flights on rumour: Hong Kong future worries Canadians.
- Prairies reap benefit of farmers' windfall: Bumper crop ripples through economy.
- Winter puts pressure on Afghan refugees: Village after village levelled as Taliban fight to keep Kabul.
- Canadian Air's work begins: The troubled airline must race against time to show the favors it has won are not in vain.
- U.S. gold deal tops $2 billion: Homestake gets Santa Fe Pacific.
- Aluminum cars face uphill drive: EV1, Prowler represent small, but significant inroads on steel's auto industry dominance.
- Stock experts still bullish, but pessimism increasing.
- Markets in upheaval: TSE fights back from a 173-point drop but still ends lower, as do bonds and C$.
- Onus now on Ottawa as CAW accepts pay cuts.
